resources.string: Record visible coordinates and follow saved waypoints

For fixed-view maps with visible integer X/Y coordinates. Not touch or video recording. Keep the same camera, movement speed and resolution. Stop normal scenario execution first. Routes are local to this device and are not included in scenario backups.
1. Select coordinate fields and map marker

Select only the X digits, then only the Y digits. Leave room for all digits; never include the comma or the other coordinate. Select a fixed map name/icon as the map marker. Move this toolbar away from these areas.

A/B measure two movement directions, not route endpoints or game objects to recognize. Recording saves where you actually walk and never clicks A/B. Replay uses the measurements to convert each waypoint into screen input.

Only calibration needs a small clear patch: stand still and choose ground about 50–120 screen pixels from the feet, then another roughly perpendicular direction. Avoid characters, buttons and walls. Observed stalls or clear detours invalidate a sample. A/B need not remain visible afterwards; record around obstacles on traversable roads.

Ground taps require a following camera and feet at the anchor. Recalibrate after camera or speed changes; waypoints remain. New obstacles and door interaction are not handled automatically.

Start and finish standing still. Walk a traversable road; slow at turns so recognition can capture them. New recordings keep old routes; drafts save every 5 seconds but cannot replay. Finer waypoints are kept, only short straight sections combined; confirm a settled corner before turning. This is not timed gesture playback. Return from near the endpoint or midway on the recorded road; no need to reach its end first.

Stand near the endpoint or on the recorded road. After locating you, the app joins that segment and follows earlier corners back to the start. It does not first go to the endpoint, cross the map directly, or change the recording.\n\nMid-route entry is restricted to the recorded corridor; distant or ambiguous parallel roads are rejected. The path must be reversible: one-way gates, drops, teleports and doors needing interaction are unsupported. It pauses if stuck. Start Replay yourself afterwards; no automatic loop.
Start/end approach: ≤ %1$.1f position units, with a traversable approach. Return can join mid-route within 1.5 units of the recorded corridor after reliable localization; no distant pathfinding.

Experimental: fixed layout, north-up, fixed zoom, player centred while the map scrolls. Select the map interior (96–512 pixels per side), excluding the border and HUD; the player must be at its centre. Rotating maps, random dungeons and moving player markers are not supported. Select a separate static map name/icon below.

Capture the reference, then test: walk slowly a short distance. Requires 20 reliable observations, at least 80% success and 12 normalized pixels of travel within 2 minutes. Return to the reference position before recording. No movement is allowed until the test passes.
Insufficient map features / unstable localization; movement disabled
Recent localization trace, up to 120 points

Fixed joystick only. Choose two perpendicular offsets beyond its deadzone, within its effective radius. Playback keeps that deflection and shortens the hold near waypoints. Change speed or hold duration? Recalibrate. Each gesture releases within 800 ms; no simultaneous attack touches.
Follow a saved route, then continue the next action

Record, test and save the route under Scenario → More → Routes first. This action follows it once, sequentially. On failure the scenario stops. Routes are local and not included in scenario backups; reselect a route after importing on another device. Split a journey into routes to insert battle or door interaction actions between segments. Timeout includes debugger pauses.
No calibrated, completed routes. Create one in Scenario → More → Routes.
Paused: position changed unexpectedly. Return to the last position.
Walk back, stand still, then tap Resume to recheck.
Recorded start: %1$s → End: %2$s\nThey can differ. Replay near the start; Return near the endpoint or from the recorded corridor.
